sleep_timeout.description: Go to sleep once no buttons have been pressed for this long, while not plugged into USB. Press the wake button to wake back up. Use 0 to never sleep.

disconnectBluetoothOnSuspend.description: When this profile's USB connection goes to sleep, disconnect the Bluetooth controllers using it so they turn off instead of running their batteries down. Turning a controller back on still wakes the PC.

invert_y_hid.label: Invert Y Axis for HID mode

syncCalibrations.label: Sync calibrations across inputs
syncCalibrations.description: Syncronise calibrations across inputs that are used multiple times. For example if you have whammy on multiple profiles, turning this on will keep your whammy calibration syncronised, while turning it off means you can have different calibrations per profile.

xinput_on_windows.label: Controller type on Windows (for USB)
xinput_on_windows.description: Pick if you wish to have your controllers emulate an XInput device or an HID device when plugged into a Windows PC. Note that this setting has no effect on macOS, Linux or on game consoles.

ps4EmulationMode.description: Pick the device type to emulate on PS4/5. PS3 works with Rock Band 4 without auth, but won't work in system menus or other games. legendMode.description: Pick the icons to show below. This adjusts the icons and names shown in the UI, such as using A or B instead of Cross and Circle

combinedStrumDebounce.label: Combined strum debounce
combinedStrumDebounce.description: Strum up and down share one debounce window, so a strum is ignored while the other direction is still held or debouncing. Stops a bouncy strum switch registering a strum in the wrong direction. While this is on, changing one strum's debounce changes them all.

queueInputs.label: Queue fret and strum inputs
queueInputs.description: Inputs are read as fast as possible and every fret / strum change is queued, then sent one at a time so the game sees every change, even ones faster than its frame rate. Adds latency while the queue drains.

dequeueInterval.label: Dequeue interval (ms)
dequeueInterval.description: How long each queued state is held for. The game needs to run at {{fps}}+ fps to see every state.

selectToDpadLeft.label: Map Select to D-pad Left on Xbox One/Series and PS4/5
selectToDpadLeft.description: Send Select as D-pad Left instead when plugged into an Xbox One/Series or PS4/5. Rock Band 4 and Fortnite Festival can use D-pad Left to activate star power, which can work better than Select.

ps3OnRpcs3.label: Use USB passthrough with RPCS3
ps3OnRpcs3.description: Switch to PS3 mode when RPCS3 detects the controller, so it can be used with RPCS3's USB passthrough. Turn this off to keep the controller in its PC mode while RPCS3 is running.

fullRangeTurntableOnPc.label: Full range scratching on PC
fullRangeTurntableOnPc.description: Real Xbox 360 turntables only send a tiny range for scratching, which XInput's default deadzone hides on PC. When enabled, scratching uses the full range on PC, and stays accurate to a real turntable when plugged into an Xbox 360.

cymbalGlitchFix.label: Apply the cymbal glitch fix
cymbalGlitchFix.description: Rock band 3 had a bug where hitting two cymbals at the same time would cause one of the cymbals to be dropped. This mitigates that bug, but may not work as well on Rock Band 2. This setting only applies on PS3 and Xbox 360.

assignments.title: Assignments
assignments.description: One of the key improvements with Santroller 2 is that you can have multiple profiles, but this means you need to tell Santroller 2 when you want your profiles used. Assignments are how this is done. Assignments come in two parts - one is the assignment itself, such as say assigning to plugging a Wii Guitar into a Wii Adapter, and the emulation type, such as USB or Bluetooth. This lets you do things like using different profiles for bluetooth vs for USB, but does mean you have to wrap your head around assignments.

direct-pico-guitar.title: Direct-Wired Guitar (Raspberry Pi Pico)
direct-pico-guitar.subtitle: Interactive Wiring & Configuration Walkthrough
direct-pico-guitar.description: Step-by-step interactive build guide for rewiring any Guitar Hero or Rock Band guitar with mechanical or original switches to a Raspberry Pi Pico or Pico 2.

intro.title: 1. Getting Started & Standard Pinout
intro.description: Prepare your tools, microcontroller, and review the standard Santroller wiring plan.
intro.familyGh: Guitar Hero (Les Paul, WT, GH5, Xplorer)
intro.welcome: This guide covers converting or rewiring a Guitar Hero or Rock Band controller to a Raspberry Pi Pico or Pico 2.
intro.directRewireCaption: A direct-wired mechanical switch guitar with a Raspberry Pi Pico
supplies: Raspberry Pi Pico 1 or Pico 2: Any standard RP2040 or RP2350 board.
Soldering iron & solder: 60/40 or lead-free.
Wire (26-30 AWG): Stranded or solid core wire.
Multimeter: Used in continuity mode (the mode that beeps when probes touch) to trace common grounds and signals.
Wire strippers & cutters: For prepping hookup wires.
rules: Find Common Ground: Use a multimeter in continuity mode to identify shared ground traces or wires.
Trace Signal Wires: Trace signal wires for each switch or potentiometer.
Solder & Verify: Solder to your chosen GP pin, then test.
intro.pinoutDesc: Use the default Santroller pin layout or choose your own GPIO pins.

frets.title: 2. Fret Buttons & Slider
frets.description: Connect the 5 fret buttons (Green, Red, Yellow, Blue, Orange) and optional touch slider bar, then verify each input in real time.
frets.intro: The frets are simple mechanical or membrane switches that share a common ground wire and have individual signal wires for each color.
frets.pcbCaption: Example neck PCB showing fret contacts and common ground trace
frets.stepGround: Identify Common Ground: If the neck cable or PCB is not labeled, inspect the neck PCB traces. One trace loops across all 5 fret switches—that is your Common Ground.
frets.stepMultimeter: Confirm with Multimeter: In continuity mode, touch one probe to common ground and the other to a fret wire. Pressing that fret should beep.
frets.stepSolderGround: Solder Common Ground: Connect the common ground wire to any GND pin on the Raspberry Pi Pico (e.g., Pin 3 or Pin 8).
frets.stepSolderSignals: Solder Fret Signals: Connect each colored fret signal wire to an unused digital GPIO pin. Our recommended standard uses:
frets.pullUpText: Santroller automatically configures internal pull-up resistors on the Pico for all digital buttons, so you do not need any external resistors. When you press a fret, it shorts the GP pin to Ground.
frets.benchHint: Assign pins manually or click Probe and press the fret button on your guitar to auto-detect its wiring:
frets.gh5Intro: Guitar Hero 5 necks feature a 4-wire digital bus that communicates over I2C. This carries the 5 fret buttons AND the capacitive touch slider bar over just two data pins plus power with zero neck modifications.
frets.gh5PinGnd: GND → Pico Pin 38 (or any GND pin)
frets.gh5VoltageWarning: Always use 3.3V (Pin 36). Never connect the neck to 5V (VBUS); doing so will permanently damage the neck controller IC.
frets.gh5DriverCardDesc: Enable Santroller's built-in GH5 neck driver to automatically configure I2C on GP18/GP19 and map both the frets and the touch slider bar.
frets.gh5DriverActive: I2C Driver Active (GP18 SDA / GP19 SCL)
frets.sliderDesc: The capacitive touch slider bar lets you tap notes in Guitar Hero and Rock Band without strumming. Touch each zone on your physical neck to verify:
frets.rbSoloIntro: Stock Rock Band guitars with solo frets use a 7-wire harness: 5 fret signal lines, 1 upper fret common, and 1 solo fret common. Santroller scans this directly as a 5x2 Matrix across 5 fret signal columns (GP2-GP6) and 2 row outputs (GP14 Upper, GP15 Solo), giving you 10 independent frets with no trace cutting required.
frets.rbSoloMatrixCols: 5 Fret Signal Columns: Green (GP2), Red (GP3), Yellow (GP4), Blue (GP5), Orange (GP6)
frets.rbSoloMatrixUpperRow: Upper Frets Common: GP14 (Pin 19) — Matrix Row 1
frets.rbSoloMatrixSoloRow: Solo Frets Common: GP15 (Pin 20) — Matrix Row 2
frets.rbSoloMatrixNoGnd: Do not connect the neck common wires to Pico GND. The Pico drives them dynamically as matrix row outputs.
frets.rbSoloDriverDesc: Enable Santroller's built-in Matrix driver to configure GP2-GP6 as column inputs and GP14/GP15 as row outputs, mapping all 10 frets automatically.
frets.rbSoloDriverActive: Matrix Driver Active (GP2-GP6 In / GP14-GP15 Out)
frets.rbShiftedIntro: Some 7-pin Rock Band necks share a common Ground with a dedicated Solo switch line. When a solo fret is pressed, it shorts both that fret's signal and the Solo line to Ground. Santroller models this via Shifted Inputs: normal frets trigger when the fret is pressed without Solo, while solo frets trigger when both are pressed.
frets.rbShiftedDriverDesc: Configure all 10 frets automatically using Shifted inputs on GP2-GP6 with GP12 as the Solo modifier.
frets.rbSplitIntro: If you have run dedicated wires from the lower neck PCB to the main body, each solo fret has its own distinct GPIO pin, allowing 10 simultaneous inputs without multiplexing.
frets.mpr121Intro: Guitar Hero World Tour guitars used a single-wire analog slider bar with high latency and limited chord detection. Bypassing the stock chip with an MPR121 capacitive touch breakout over I2C provides ultra-low latency multi-touch tracking.
frets.mpr121StepTraces: Cut traces leading away from chip U2 (or desolder U2 entirely) on the slider PCB as shown in the diagram.
frets.mpr121TracesCaption: Trace cuts around U2 on the World Tour slider PCB
frets.mpr121StepVias: Solder wires from each via (channels 0 through 4) on the slider PCB to channels 0-4 on the MPR121 breakout.
frets.mpr121ViasCaption: Slider via locations to solder to MPR121 channels 0-4
frets.mpr121StepFrets: Connect the 5 fret signal wires to MPR121 channels 5-9, or wire them directly to Pico GPIOs GP2-GP6.
frets.mpr121StepI2c: Connect the MPR121 to the Pico over I2C: 3.3V (Pin 36), GND (Pin 38), SDA (GP18 / Pin 24), and SCL (GP19 / Pin 25).

strum.title: 3. Strum Bar Switches
strum.description: Connect Strum Up and Strum Down switches, cut board traces if reusing original PCBs, and test switch actuation.
strum.intro: The strum bar is operated by two switches: Strum Up and Strum Down. Like the frets, these two switches share a common ground wire.
strum.strumPcbCaption: Strum switches on an original main PCB
strum.directIntro: When using replacement mechanical switches (like Kailh Box switches) or a 3D-printed strum bracket, the switches are completely isolated from stock circuitry.
strum.directStepGround: Common Ground: Connect one pin of each switch together and wire to any GND pin on the Pico.
strum.directStepUp: Strum Up: Connect the signal contact to GP7 (Pin 10).
strum.directStepDown: Strum Down: Connect the signal contact to GP8 (Pin 11).
strum.cutTraceDesc1: If your strum switches are soldered directly to an original console PCB (such as Wii, Xbox 360, or PS3), they remain connected to the original console microcontroller and capacitors. This causes phantom or stuck inputs unless traces are cut.
strum.cutTraceDesc2: Use a craft knife or razor to score and sever the copper traces leading away from the switch pins. Use your multimeter in continuity mode to confirm each switch contact is isolated from the rest of the board.
strum.cutTraceCaption: Cutting copper traces around strum switch contacts
strum.benchHint: Assign pins manually or flick the strum bar to auto-detect the switch:
strum.debounceDesc: Mechanical strum switches can bounce on release, causing unwanted double strums. You can fine-tune Strum Debounce in Profile Poll Settings if you notice accidental over-strums.

whammy.title: 4. Whammy Bar Potentiometer
whammy.description: Wire the 10k potentiometer to 3.3V, Ground, and ADC0 (GP26), then test live analog movement.
whammy.intro: The whammy bar connects to an analog potentiometer (typically 10kΩ). Unlike digital buttons which are on or off, the whammy measures variable depth and must connect to one of the Pico's dedicated Analog ADC pins.
whammy.potCenter: Center Pin (Signal / Wiper): Solder to GP26 (ADC0 / Pin 31) on your Pico.
whammy.potOuter1: Outer Pin 1: Solder to 3V3(OUT) (Pin 36) on your Pico.
whammy.potOuter2: Outer Pin 2: Solder to GND (Pin 38) on your Pico.
whammy.invertNote: (Note: If the whammy value decreases when pressed instead of increasing, you can either swap the two outer wires or toggle "Invert" in calibration.)
whammy.warning2WireDesc: Some stock guitars have a potentiometer PCB where two pins are bridged, leaving only 2 wires exposed. You must desolder the bridged connection and solder 3 distinct wires directly to the 3 potentiometer pins.
whammy.warning2WireCaption: Desoldering bridged pins to wire 3 full lines (3V3, Signal, GND)
whammy.pickupIntro: Rock Band Stratocaster and Precision Bass guitars include a 5-way pickup selector switch for guitar effects. Like the whammy, it connects to an analog ADC pin (GP27 / ADC1).

tilt.digitalMount: Mount the sensor inside the guitar body angled slightly upward towards the neck.
tilt.i2cIntro: Accelerometers measure gravitational acceleration along 3 axes for tilt detection.
tilt.benchHint: Tilt the guitar body upward to test activation:

nav.description: Wire the Start and Select buttons to GP9 and GP10, and optionally configure the Home combo.

nav.startSignal: Start Button Signal: Connect the Start signal wire to GP9 (Pin 12).
nav.selectSignal: Select Button Signal: Connect the Select signal wire to GP10 (Pin 14).

ps2-wiring.title: 2. Solder Wires & Enable Driver
ps2-wiring.description: Connect the 6 signal and power wires and enable the PS2 controller driver.
solderingSteps: Solder Clock (SCK): Connect PS2 Pin 5 to GP6 (Pin 9).
Solder Command (MOSI): Connect PS2 Pin 2 to GP3 (Pin 5).
Solder Data (MISO) & Resistor: Connect PS2 Pin 1 to GP4 (Pin 6). Place a 1kΩ resistor between GP4 and 3V3 (Pin 36).
Solder Acknowledge & Resistor: Connect PS2 Pin 9 to GP7 (Pin 10). Place a 1kΩ resistor between GP7 and 3V3 (Pin 36).
Solder Attention (ATT): Connect PS2 Pin 6 to GP10 (Pin 14).
Power & Ground: Connect PS2 Pin 4 to 3V3(OUT) (Pin 36) and PS2 Pin 7 to GND (Pin 38).

tt-wiring.title: 2. Platter & Crossfader Wiring
tt-wiring.description: Wire the optical encoder, platter buttons, crossfader, and effects dial.
wiringSteps: Platter Encoder (I2C): Locate the platter connector pads labelled V, G, C, and D. Connect V to 3V3(OUT), G to GND, C to GP19 (SCL), and D to GP18 (SDA).

supportedHardware.title: Supported Hardware
supportedHardware.subtitle: Comprehensive catalog of all microcontrollers, USB host devices, sensors, and accessories compatible with Santroller.
supportedHardware.alertBody: Santroller turns a Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040 or RP2350) into an all-in-one controller hub. You can wire custom buttons, switches, and LEDs directly to GPIO pins, read legacy console buses (like Wii and PS2 controllers), or use the secondary USB Host port to connect modern wireless dongles, authentic controllers, and authentication keys.
supportedHardware.cloneWarningTitle: Buyer Beware: Counterfeit AliExpress "Pico W" Clones
supportedHardware.cloneWarningBody: Many ultra-cheap "Pico W" boards sold on AliExpress and similar marketplaces are knock-offs that replace the official Infineon CYW43439 chip with an obsolete ESP8266 or ESP8285 Wi-Fi microcontroller. The ESP8266/ESP8285 has NO Bluetooth hardware whatsoever. Because Santroller relies on Bluetooth Classic for wireless controllers and Wii Remote emulation, these clone boards will NEVER work with Santroller Bluetooth. Always ensure your board is an authentic Raspberry Pi Pico W / Pico 2 W featuring the official silver metal RF shield stamped with the Raspberry Pi logo.

switches_mechanical.name: Mechanical & Arcade Switches
switches_mechanical.description: Wire mechanical switches directly to the Pico pins with hardware debouncing in firmware.
details: Compatible with Cherry MX, Kailh Box, Gateron, and Kailh Low-Profile Choc switches
Original guitar fret silicon membranes and strum microswitches
Internal pull-up resistors enabled automatically (wire switch between GPIO and GND)
Configurable debouncing algorithm to eliminate double-strums and ghost notes

analog_whammy_joystick.name: Potentiometers, Hall Sensors & Joysticks
analog_whammy_joystick.description: Connect analog potentiometers or contactless Hall-effect sensors to measure whammy bar angle or joystick position.
details: 10k Ohm linear potentiometers for whammy bars
Hall-effect magnetic angle sensors for wear-free contactless whammy
2-axis analog thumbstick modules with integrated push button
Piezoelectric transducers with conditioning circuit for electronic drum pads

sensors_tilt_imu.name: Tilt Sensors & Digital Accelerometers
sensors_tilt_imu.description: Trigger Star Power / Overdrive naturally by tilting the neck of your guitar up.
details: Mechanical ball-roll / mercury tilt switches wired to digital GPIO
Digital I2C Accelerometers / IMUs (MPU6050, ADXL345) for smooth gesture detection
Configurable angle threshold and tilt sensitivity in the Configurator

periph_gh5_neck.name: Guitar Hero 5 / Band Hero Detachable Neck
periph_gh5_neck.description: Native digital support for the GH5 / Band Hero neck board. Communicates directly over the original 4-pin neck connector without modifying the neck PCB.
details: Reads 5 frets and the touch-sensitive solo slider strip digitally over I2C
Uses original spring-pin contacts (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL)
Preserves detachable neck functionality on Guitar Hero 5 and Band Hero guitars

periph_crkd_neck.name: CRKD Nitro Deck / Guitar Neck Board
periph_crkd_neck.description: Serial protocol support for CRKD guitar necks powered by the PY32F002B ARM microcontroller.
details: High-speed 460.8 kbps serial stream with CRC-8 Maxim/Dow integrity verification
Transmits 5 frets, solo tap frets, and neck D-pad axes in a compact frame
Supports CRKD neck WS2812 addressable LED pass-through

periph_protar_neck.name: Mad Catz Rock Band 3 Pro Guitar Neck
periph_protar_neck.description: Custom SPI communication driver for the 102-button Rock Band 3 Mustang and Squier Pro Guitar necks.
details: Scans all 17 frets across all 6 strings (102 discrete fret switches)
Reads frets, fretboard solo flags, and navigation buttons
Connects via MOSI, MISO, SCK, and Attention / Chip Select pins

periph_crazy_guitar.name: Crazy Guitar / RedOctane Custom Neck
periph_crazy_guitar.description: Direct protocol support for Crazy Guitar neck boards communicating over standard 2-wire I2C.
details: 5-fret digital decoding directly from neck microprocessor
Compatible with 3.3V and 5V signaling topologies

periph_wt_drum.name: Guitar Hero World Tour Drum Module
periph_wt_drum.description: Interfacing driver for the internal SPI microprocessor on Guitar Hero World Tour drum kits.
details: Reads velocity and hit triggers from 3 drum pads, 2 cymbals, and bass kick pedal
Wires to SPI bus with dedicated Chip Select line

periph_bh_drum.name: Band Hero / Guitar Hero 5 Drum Module
periph_bh_drum.description: I2C protocol communication for Band Hero and GH5 drum brain electronics.
details: Decodes dynamic velocity data from drum pads and cymbals over I2C
Allows reusing stock Band Hero drum hardware without replacing piezo sensors

periph_crkd_drum.name: CRKD Electronic Drum Interface
periph_crkd_drum.description: High-speed UART communication for CRKD drum kit modules with digital trigger reporting.
details: Direct hardware serial connection for drum hit reporting
Low-latency drum pad, cymbal, and kick pedal event stream

periph_djh_turntable.name: DJ Hero Turntable Platter Sub-Module
periph_djh_turntable.description: Direct I2C protocol reader for the detachable turntable platter mechanism from DJ Hero controllers.
details: Reads optical quadrature wheel ticks, 3 stream buttons (Green/Red/Blue), and 360° rotation
Configurable left-hand or right-hand platter orientation and 5 ms polling interval

periph_infinium_fader.name: Infinium Optical Contactless Crossfader
periph_infinium_fader.description: Ultra-precise optical crossfader interface used in professional DJ mixers and custom scratch builds.
details: Wear-free contactless optical sensor tracking with infinite lifespan
Serial data stream polled at zero latency for razor-sharp crossfader cuts

periph_vtech_guitar.name: VTech KidiStar Guitar I/O Expander
periph_vtech_guitar.description: Specialized SPI expander protocol for converting toy and rhythm instruments into full-featured Santroller controllers.
details: Dedicated SPI driver with interrupt/attention signaling
Decodes matrixed buttons and fret switches into individual game actions

periph_secondary_pico.name: Secondary Pi Pico (I2C Coprocessor)
periph_secondary_pico.description: Put a second Raspberry Pi Pico in your guitar neck to scan frets and sensors with zero latency, sharing data over I2C with the main Pico.
details: Secondary Pico runs Santroller Peripheral firmware in the neck or secondary enclosure
Allows ultra-clean 4-wire neck quick-disconnects (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL)
Offloads GPIO button scanning, matrix routing, or LEDs across a high-speed bus

exp_mpr121.name: MPR121 Capacitive Touch & Slider Sensor
exp_mpr121.description: 12-channel capacitive touch sensor. The gold-standard solution for rewiring the Guitar Hero World Tour touch slider bar.
details: 12 independent capacitive electrode channels with auto-calibration
Channels 0-4 map to the 5 touch slider segments; remaining channels can poll frets
Drastically reduces latency and improves reliability over the stock WT slider circuit

exp_multiplexer.name: Analog / Digital Multiplexers (CD4051 & CD4067)
exp_multiplexer.description: Expand a single GPIO or ADC pin into 8 or 16 inputs using affordable CD74HC4051 (8-ch) or CD74HC4067 (16-ch) multiplexers.
details: CD4051: 8 channels controlled with 3 address pins (S0-S2) and 1 input line
CD4067: 16 channels controlled with 4 address pins (S0-S3) and 1 input line
Compatible with analog inputs (potentiometers/whammy) and digital buttons
Built-in configurable scanning loop in Santroller firmware

exp_matrix_switch_network.name: Key Matrix & Switch Networks (Dioded)
exp_matrix_switch_network.description: Scan dozens of buttons and mechanical switches using minimal pins via row-and-column matrix scanning or resister networks.
details: Up to 32-pin matrix configurations with anti-ghosting diode support
Switch Network driver for decoded button networks
Ideal for arcade panels, dance stages, and full keyboard layouts

exp_ads1115.name: ADS1115 16-Bit Precision ADC
exp_ads1115.description: Ultra-high precision 16-bit analog-to-digital converter for studio-grade analog whammy, analog stick, and piezo velocity tracking.
details: 4 single-ended or 2 differential high-precision analog channels
Programmable gain amplifier and hardware interrupt line
Provides far superior noise rejection and resolution compared to standard 10/12-bit ADCs

exp_rotary_encoder.name: Hardware Quadrature Rotary Encoders
exp_rotary_encoder.description: High-speed optical and mechanical rotary encoder decoding for DJ Hero platters, volume dials, and spinner wheels.
details: Hardware interrupt and PIO edge tracking prevents dropped ticks at high spin speeds
Sub-tick direction discrimination and configurable sensitivity multiplier

led_addressable_rgb.name: Addressable RGB LEDs (WS2812B / Neopixels)
led_addressable_rgb.description: High-speed addressable LED strip and individual LED support driven seamlessly by RP2040 PIO.
details: Supports WS2812B, SK6812 (RGBW), and WS2813 LED strips
Under-fret lighting: Frets light up with their respective note colors when pressed
Reactive strum lighting and Star Power / Overdrive full-body illumination
Player number indicators and idle animation patterns

led_apa102.name: APA102 / DotStar High-Speed SPI LEDs
led_apa102.description: Two-wire SPI addressable LEDs capable of multi-megahertz refresh rates without timing jitter.
details: Hardware SPI driven up to 12 MHz for flicker-free persistence-of-vision effects
Separate Data (MOSI) and Clock (SCK) lines prevent color timing glitches
RGB and BGR byte order configurations

led_stp16cpc.name: STP16CPC26 Constant-Current LED Driver
led_stp16cpc.description: 16-channel constant-current LED sink driver for lighting original guitar LEDs, button backlights, or arcade lamps.
details: 16 constant-current sink outputs with single-resistor global current setting
Controlled via SPI (MOSI, SCK, LE Latch, OE Output Enable)
Eliminates per-LED resistors; ideal for custom PCB faceplates and illuminated frets

led_dmx512.name: DMX512 Stage Lighting Interface
led_dmx512.description: Control real professional stage lights, smoke machines, and strobe fixtures synchronized to your gameplay in real time.
details: Generates genuine DMX512 packet timing (250 kbps RS-485 stream)
Outputs lighting triggers for notes hit, streaks, star power, and game state
Turn your living room or stage into an authentic concert experience while playing

led_discrete.name: Discrete Single-Color LEDs
led_discrete.description: Drive original faceplate LEDs, player indicator lights, or custom LEDs with current-limiting resistors.
details: Player 1-4 indicator LEDs
Star Power / Overdrive alert LEDs
Low battery warning indicator (on Pico W wireless builds)

pwr_max1704x.name: MAX17043 / MAX17048 Fuel Gauge IC
pwr_max1704x.description: Dedicated LiPo / Li-Ion battery fuel gauge IC utilizing Maxim ModelGauge algorithm for accurate state-of-charge tracking.
details: Reports cell voltage and battery percentage directly over I2C
Alert pin threshold triggers when battery drops below low power limit
Provides accurate battery reporting to game consoles (PS3, PS4, Switch, Wii)

pwr_adc_battery.name: ADC Voltage Divider Battery Monitor
pwr_adc_battery.description: Monitor single-cell LiPo battery voltage using the Raspberry Pi Pico onboard 3:1 voltage divider circuit.
details: GP29 measures VSYS battery supply voltage (3.3V empty to 4.2V full cell)
Configurable voltage divider ratio and millivolt thresholds in Configurator
Triggers console low-battery indicators and sleep routines without extra ICs

pwr_management_sleep.name: Power Management & Inactivity Sleep
pwr_management_sleep.description: Advanced firmware power saving that cuts power to external LED strips, peripherals, or sleep ICs during inactivity.
details: Periodic heartbeat pulse pin to keep external power banks awake
Inactivity timeout pin drives high/low to shut down MOSFET switches and save battery
Wakes instantly on any fret, strum, or button press

bus_wii_extension.name: Wii Extension Bus (I2C Input)
bus_wii_extension.description: Read authentic Wii Guitar Hero guitars, drums, or Nunchuks directly through the 6-pin Wii extension connector.
details: No need to gut your Wii guitar: plugs straight into the Wii Remote extension cable
Reads frets, strum bar, whammy, joystick, and touch slider over standard 3.3V I2C
Allows creating a standalone plug-and-play USB adapter for Wii rhythm controllers

bus_wii_emulation.name: Wii Extension Port Emulation (Hardware Bus)
bus_wii_emulation.description: Emulate a physical Wii Extension device (Guitar Hero guitar or Classic Controller) to plug Santroller directly into a genuine Wii Remote!
details: Santroller acts as the I2C peripheral speaking the encrypted Nintendo extension protocol
Plugs into physical Wii Remotes to play Wii Guitar Hero games wirelessly on consoles

bus_ps2_controller.name: PlayStation 1 & 2 Controller Bus (SPI Input)
bus_ps2_controller.description: Directly read original PS1/PS2 DualShock controllers and Guitar Hero SG guitars via their native serial bus.
details: Compatible with PS2 Guitar Hero SG guitars and standard DualShock 2 controllers
Reads button pressure levels and analog stick data with microsecond accuracy
Builds a zero-lag USB adapter for original PS2 rhythm controllers

bus_ps2_emulation.name: PlayStation 1 & 2 Port Emulation (Output)
bus_ps2_emulation.interfaceType: SPI Pins (CMD, ATT, ACK, DATA, CLK)
bus_ps2_emulation.description: Santroller natively emulates a physical PS1/PS2 controller, allowing you to plug your custom instrument into original PlayStation hardware.
details: Full 5-wire hardware emulation of DualShock and Guitar Hero SG controllers
Connects directly to the PS1/PS2 console controller ports with zero latency

bus_snes_pad.name: Super Nintendo (SNES) / NES Controller Bus
bus_snes_pad.description: Direct support for reading Super Nintendo and NES gamepads and rhythm accessories.
details: Reads standard 4021 shift-register serial gamepads over Clock, Latch, and Data lines
Sub-millisecond shift register latching directly into Santroller inputs

bus_joybus.name: Nintendo Joybus (N64 & GameCube Controller Bus)
bus_joybus.description: Direct bidirectional communication with original Nintendo 64 and Nintendo GameCube controllers.
details: Single-wire bidirectional Joybus protocol driven with RP2040 PIO
Reads original GameCube controllers, DK Bongos, and N64 gamepads with microsecond timing

bus_joybus_emulation.name: GameCube / Joybus Port Emulation (Output)
bus_joybus_emulation.description: Santroller can emulate a native GameCube controller, enabling you to plug directly into GameCube and Wii GC controller ports.
details: Works with GameCube consoles, Wii GameCube ports, and Smash Bros USB adapters
Native Joybus response timing generated via high-speed PIO state machines

bus_xbox360_rf.name: Xbox 360 RF Wireless Module (Front Panel)
bus_xbox360_rf.description: Wire the front-panel RF board harvested from an Xbox 360 Fat or Slim console to Santroller to build a standalone wireless receiver!
details: Supports Xbox 360 Fat and Slim RF daughterboards
Reads wireless controllers, wireless guitars, and wireless drums directly over RF
Supports the hardware SYNC button and animated Ring of Light LED status

bus_midi.name: MIDI 5-Pin DIN & USB-MIDI Devices
bus_midi.description: Interface professional electronic drum kits, MIDI keyboards, or synthesizers directly to Santroller.
details: Standard 5-pin DIN MIDI IN with optocoupler circuit via hardware UART (31,250 baud)
USB-MIDI instruments plugged into Santroller USB Host port

Map MIDI note numbers and velocity directly to Rock Band Pro Drum pads and cymbals

features: Compatible with all Guitar Hero games across PS3, 360, Wii
Supports touch slider / solo strip on compatible guitars
Full whammy axis calibration and deadzone controls

Overdrive Integration: Enable 'Select to D-pad Left' in profile options for instant Star Power in game.

wiiBluetooth.title: Nintendo Wii & Wii U: Wireless Wii Remote Emulation (Recommended)
wiiBluetooth.subtitle: Connect natively via Bluetooth with ZERO console modifications, plugins, or homebrew
wiiBluetooth.alertBody: Modern Santroller firmware can emulate an entire wireless Nintendo Wii Remote directly over Bluetooth. This allows you to play Guitar Hero, Band Hero, and DJ Hero on completely stock Wii and Wii U consoles running real retail game discs, without needing Brainslug or homebrew.
wiiBluetooth.hardwarePicoW: Raspberry Pi Pico W / Pico 2 W: Built-in CYW43439 Bluetooth radio emulates the Wii Remote wirelessly.
wiiBluetooth.hardwarePicoWWarning: * Warning: Avoid knockoff AliExpress "Pico W" boards that use an ESP8285/ESP8266 chip. They lack Bluetooth hardware and will not work!
wiiBluetooth.hardwareDongle: Standard Pico + USB Host BT Dongle: Plug a CSR8510 or BCM20702 Bluetooth adapter into your Pico's USB host port.
pairingSteps: Configure your device in Santroller Configurator with Wii Remote Emulation enabled.
Power on your instrument and your Nintendo Wii / Wii U console.
Press the red SYNC button on the Wii console, then press SYNC on your controller.
The controller connects as Player 1 (or 2/3/4) and behaves as a genuine Wii Remote with guitar/drum extension!

brainslug.title: Nintendo Wii: Santroller Brainslug (Alternative / USB Option)
brainslug.subtitle: Allows Guitar Hero, Band Hero, and DJ Hero on Wii to recognize wired USB instruments as Wii Remotes
brainslug.intro: If you are using a wired USB controller without Bluetooth hardware, Guitar Hero and DJ Hero on Wii expect guitars to be plugged into a Wii Remote extension port. Santroller Brainslug is a custom homebrew module that intercepts game controller routines and routes USB instruments directly to the game!
brainslug.discTitle: Setup with Real Game Discs (Homebrew Channel)
discSteps: Extract the contents of sd.zip directly to the root of your Wii SD card.
Plug your Santroller USB instrument into the Wii USB port.
Insert your game disc and launch the Homebrew Channel.
Launch Brainslug from the Homebrew Channel. The game will boot with USB instrument support enabled.
brainslug.usbLoaderTitle: Setup with USB Loader GX (USB Hard Drive Games)
brainslug.usbLoaderAlertBody: You must run the game from a USB hard drive/flash drive. Booting games from an SD card locks the card and prevents Brainslug from loading its modules.
usbLoaderSteps: Extract sd.zip to the root of your SD card.
In /bcs/dols/, rename RGHE52.dol to the Title ID of the game you want to play (e.g., SXEE52.dol for Guitar Hero 5). You can duplicate and rename the file for multiple games.
Select your Guitar Hero game and click Settings → Game Load.
Set Custom Game IOS to 249 (or your cIOS slot).
Save settings, plug in your USB instrument, and launch the game!

pademu.title: PlayStation 2: PADEMU in Open PS2 Loader (OPL)
pademu.subtitle: Emulate standard PS2 controller inputs from USB instruments on modded PS2 consoles
pademu.intro: Because early PS2 games (such as Guitar Hero 1 & 2 and standard gamepads) only recognize controllers wired to the front DualShock ports, they ignore standard USB inputs. PADEMU (Pad Emulator) built into Open PS2 Loader translates USB controllers into virtual PS2 controllers in software!
pademu.note: Note: Santroller firmware automatically enters PS3 mode when plugged into a PS2. PADEMU detects PS3 guitars and emulates an authentic PS2 Guitar Hero SG controller automatically. PADEMU works with ISO/backup games booted through OPL (not retail disc booting).
steps: Plug your Santroller guitar or controller into a PS2 USB port.
Plug an original PS2 controller into Port 2 (useful for backup menu navigation).
Ensure you are running a recent build of <extlink>Open PS2 Loader (OPL) <icon /></extlink>.
Launch OPL and press Start to open Settings.
Set Settings For Port to 1P and set Emulation to On.
Launch Guitar Hero or any standard PS2 game from OPL. Your USB instrument will now work!

orbis.title: Modded Console Plugins: PS4 OrbisInstrumentalizer

orbis.cardBody: Patches Rock Band 4 and Guitar Hero Live to remove instrument restrictions and authentication checks, allowing any USB guitar or drum controller to work without needing an authentic security controller plugged into the USB Host port.

auth.alertBody: Modern consoles (Xbox One, Xbox Series, PS4, PS5) challenge connected USB controllers with cryptographic challenges every few minutes. If a controller cannot sign the challenge using an official private key, the console disables or disconnects it after 8 minutes.

builtIn.title: 1. Built-in Keys
builtIn.body: Santroller includes built-in security keys for the Xbox 360. It passes the Xbox 360 security handshake natively without requiring an external dongle or setup.

usbPassthrough.title: 2. USB Passthrough
usbPassthrough.body: Connect an official controller or most third-party Xbox One gamepads / security dongles into the secondary USB Host port. Santroller transparently passes challenges through while you play.

harvestedChip.title: 3. Harvested Chip (I2C)
harvestedChip.body: Harvest the security authentication chip from an Xbox One controller PCB and wire it directly to the Pico via I2C. Enables fully internal, dongle-free Xbox One/Series authentication!

noAuth.title: 4. No-Auth Modes
noAuth.body:
Use protocol modes that do not require authentication:
• Fortnite Festival: Keyboard Profiles
• Rock Band 4 on PS4/PS5: Legacy PS3 mode

auth.hardwareTitle: Supported Security Hardware for Xbox & PlayStation
auth.hardwareSubtitle: When USB Host inputs or an I2C Xbox One auth chip are configured, authentication challenges from the console are automatically handled:

xbone.hardware: Official or most 3rd-party wired Xbox One/Series gamepads, OR harvested Xbox One auth chip (I2C)
xbone.notes: Most third-party Xbox One gamepads are supported over USB Host. Alternatively, solder a harvested Xbox One security chip directly to Pico I2C pins for an internal, dongle-free build.

ps4.hardware: DualShock 4 or Mayflash MAGPS4 / Magicboots PS4 dongle
ps4.notes: Keep the dongle or controller connected while playing.

festival.alertBody: In modern Santroller firmware, Fortnite Festival is no longer a rigid, hardcoded mode. Instead, you set it up by creating Profiles! This gives you full freedom to configure your own custom keybindings, choose between keyboard and controller emulation, and play on consoles without needing any authentication dongles.

keyboard.title: Why Use a Keyboard Profile on Consoles?
keyboard.subtitle: Bypasses all console controller authentication without extra hardware!
keyboard.body1: Consoles (PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X|S) enforce strict cryptographic security handshakes on gamepads, causing unauthenticated devices to disconnect after 8 minutes.
keyboard.body2: However, all modern consoles natively accept USB keyboards without any authentication checks. By creating a Keyboard Profile in Santroller, your guitar or drum controller acts as a standard keyboard—allowing you to play Fortnite Festival natively with zero timeouts and no security dongles!
keyboard.badge: Works on PS4, PS5, Xbox One & Series

pc.title: Playing on PC / Windows
pc.subtitle: Choose between native controller mode or keyboard emulation
pc.body: On PC, Fortnite Festival supports both native guitar controllers and standard keyboards:
options: Native Guitar Mode: Use a standard Guitar Hero or Rock Band profile with XInput enabled. Enable Send Select as D-pad Left in Profile Options so Overdrive activates properly.
Keyboard Mode: Use a Keyboard profile if you prefer binding custom keys or matching PC keyboard rhythm setups.

steps.title: Step-by-Step: Creating a Fortnite Festival Profile
steps.subtitle: Follow these steps to create and customize your Fortnite Festival setup in the new configurator:
steps.addProfile: Add a New Profile: In the sidebar under the Profiles section, click Add profile. Name it something clear, such as Fortnite Keyboard.
steps.setEmulation: Set Emulation Type to Keyboard: In your profile's options, set Device to Emulate to Keyboard / Mouse.
steps.loadPreset: Load a Mapping Preset (Optional Quickstart): Under the Mappings section, select Presets to populate default bindings:
presets: Fortnite Festival - Guitar (Lead): Binds frets to D, F, J, K, L and Overdrive to Space.
Fortnite Festival - Pro Guitar: Binds frets to 1-5, strums to Right Shift / Right Ctrl, whammy to Slash, and tilt to PageDown.
Fortnite Festival - Drums / Pro Drums: Binds pads and cymbals to standard drum keys.
steps.customize: Customize Your Own Key Bindings: You are not locked into the presets! Click any input row to bind your frets, strum bar, whammy bar, or tilt sensor to whatever keys you prefer in your in-game Fortnite settings.
steps.navigation: Add Menu Navigation Bindings: In the new firmware, you can bind navigation keys (such as Arrow keys, Enter, or Escape) to dedicated buttons or button shortcuts (e.g. Start + Select) so you can navigate Fortnite's menus with ease.
steps.assignments: Set Profile Assignments (Triggers): Under Assignments, configure when this profile activates. You can set an activation trigger to hold a button (like the Green fret or Start button) while plugging in to switch into this profile, or set it as default.
steps.save: Save to Device: Click Save Settings. Your controller will now output your custom keyboard bindings when plugged in!
